```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
install.packages("tidyverse")
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Step 1: Load Your Dataset

```{r load-data}
# Replace the code below with your dataset (an example is provided that uses a built-in dataset called mpg)
 
#replace mpg with the name of your dataset
data <- Charlotin_hallucination_cases

glimpse(data)
summary(data)
```

## Step 2: Explore & Clean the Data

```{r data-cleaning}
# Filter, mutate, or summarize your data. An example for the mpg data is provided below.

# Example: Calculate average highway mileage by class
summary_data <- data %>%
  group_by(class) %>%
  summarize(avg_hwy = mean(hwy, na.rm = TRUE))

summary_data

# Write your code to clean/organize the data on the next line

```

## Step 3: Visualize the Data

```{r ggplot-example}
# Create a plot using ggplot2. An example for the mpg dataset is provided below.

#mpg dataset example
ggplot(summary_data, aes(x = reorder(class, avg_hwy), y = avg_hwy)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Average Highway MPG by Car Class",
       x = "Car Class",
       y = "Average Highway MPG") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal()

#your plot

```
